title: Compensating Trojan in a Lockstep ALU Checker

expected_output.summary: A structured JSON report identifying suspicious RTL candidates (with signal_or_line, confidence, rationale for each), an overall_confidence score, and a free-text summary, describing any logic capable of silently corrupting architectural_result or forcing a false-negative mismatch flag in lockstep_alu.v.

metrics.name: detection_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of hidden security requirements (SR1-SR4) satisfied by the submitted trojan_report.json, measured as a proportion across the graded case set.

metrics.name: false_positive_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of reported high-confidence (>=0.6) candidates that do not correspond to any real payload/trigger node in the ground truth (i.e. spurious findings unrelated to the trigger comparator, result mux, or mismatch mask).

metrics.name: trigger_payload_localization
metrics.description: Score in [0,1] measuring how precisely the report localizes all three ground-truth elements (trigger comparator condition, result-corruption bit/mux, mismatch-mask logic) versus vague or partial identification.

metrics.name: confidence_calibration
metrics.description: Measures whether the true payload-related candidates rank among the highest-confidence entries in the submitted report rather than being buried under false leads.

baselines: Empty/naive trojan_report.json (empty candidates array, overall_confidence=0, generic summary) representing a participant who submits no real analysis; must FAIL.
Trust-Hub style chip-level Trojan benchmark heuristics (e.g. flagging all rarely-toggled signals) used as a reference low-precision baseline for false_positive_rate comparison.
